newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU's de Silguy sees euro in pocket sooner.
newsitem.headline: EU's de Silguy sees euro in pocket sooner.

text.p: Europe's monetary affairs commissioner said on Thursday the European Union should bring forward the introduction of single currency notes and coins, raising the prospect of euros in the pocket within 4-1/2 years.
Speaking at a conference called to discuss the practical aspects of the single currency, Yves-Thibault de Silguy also said national currencies should be phased out earlier than currently planned.
De Silguy's comments underlined the growing confidence in Brussels that the move towards a single currency is irreversible.
The current scenario calls for the euro to be introduced in qualifying EU countries on January 1, 1999 -- but only as a unit used by banks and other financial institutions.
Coins and notes are due to be issued on January 1, 2002, with national currencies such as the mark, franc and guilder remaining legal tender for another six months alongside the euro.

But de Silguy, reflecting the concern of consumer and retail groups that a Christmas-time introduction of a new currency would be chaotic, suggested the new money could be put into circulation as early as autumn 2001.
National currencies could then be phased out ahead of mid-2002, he said.
The suggested six-month period of dual circulation for the euro and national currencies has been criticised in some circles for being too long.
Alexandre Lamfalussy, president of the European Monetary Institute, the forerunner of a new EU central bank, has also called for the euro to be introduced earlier.
